sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:192445
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 44942 of 2024

Applicant :- Gyanmati
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Rajeev Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Rajeev Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned
Aga-I for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime
No. 569 of 2024, under Sections 85, 61(2), 124(1), 80 B.N.S. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station
Pipraich, District Gorakhpur during pendency of the trial.

3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, she has been made accused in the present matter along with her other family members including husband of the deceased.
4.

He further submits that there is dying declaration of the deceased recorded by the Tehsildar concerned, which has been annexed at page-59 of the paper-book and from its perusal it reflects, the allegation of ablazing the deceased was against her husband i.e. son of the applicant and from the perusal of the dying declaration, it reflects that Devrani of the deceased provided match stick to the Gyanmati vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171852422/
1 husband of the deceased.
He next argued there is no allegation that applicant anyhow participated in the alleged incident of ablazing.

5. He further submits, only allegation against the applicant in the dying declaration is that she also along with her son used to make demand of dowry but on the basis of such allegation at the worst applicant can only be prosecuted for offence under Section 498A IPC and it cannot be said that applicant caused dowry death of her daughter-in-law as specific role of causing burn injury to the deceased has been attributed by her to her husband i.e. son of the applicant.

6. He further submits, however, apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal history of a case under Section 498A IPC but in that case due to matrimonial dispute arose between husband and wife, applicant has been made accused and criminal history of the applicant has been explained in paragraph-25 of the affidavit filed in support of instant bail application.
7. He further submits that applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and in the present matter she is in jail since 13.09.2024.
8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Considering the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant and the dying declaration of the deceased recorded by the Tehsildar concerned, which has been annexed at page-59 of the paper-book and the fact that applicant is a lady and her criminal history of solitary case has been explained in the instant bail application and in the present matter she is in jail since 13.09.2024, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Gyanmati be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

Gyanmati vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171852422/
2 13.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 9.12.2024 AK Pandey  Gyanmati vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171852422/
